justin_ending_beside.070: Justin counts you both in, under his breath. Not in eights. Just *one, two* — and then he stops counting, because you're already in step.
justin_ending_someday.001: For a second he just looks at you. Then he understands which slow part you mean, and the understanding goes through him like a count-in.
justin_ending_someday.004: Good. I've got about thirty seconds and I don't want to spend them badly.
justin_ending_someday.005: Roof. After. I want to say it properly, where I can see your face.
justin_ending_someday.006: WRITING RECORD 07 TO KEEPSAKE. TYPE: VIDEO. AUDIO TRACK: NONE.
justin_ending_someday.007: I also observed forty seconds of conversation which I agreed not to log.
justin_ending_someday.008: I have filed it as: UNRESOLVED, BY MUTUAL AGREEMENT. It is a new category. It is already my favourite.
justin_ending_someday.009: "By mutual agreement"? ECHO, what did they say?
justin_ending_someday.010: It said it didn't log it. Leave the building alone. It's had a long night.
justin_ending_someday.011: Songha's pen is moving, though. You catch the word *November* before he closes the notebook.
justin_ending_someday.012: It's a good record. You can hear the counting, if you watch his mouth.
justin_ending_someday.015: A glass card slides out of a slot in the front desk you never knew was there. Warm. The size of a playing card. Inside it, very small, someone is dancing.
justin_ending_someday.016: You hold it. I'd only keep checking my footwork.
justin_ending_someday.017: The roof looks different with the sky on. The bench is still there. So is the dent your coat left in the dust at one end of it.
justin_ending_someday.018: The others have gone to find breakfast. Songha said *ten minutes* to the two of you in a voice that meant *take twenty*.
justin_ending_someday.019: Justin stands at the rail. Not bouncing. You put the glass card on the bench between you, and it catches the first real light and throws a small red square on the concrete.
justin_ending_someday.020: Zero fingers. Hold me to it.
justin_ending_someday.021: You hold up a closed fist. He looks at it and nods, like a dancer taking a mark.
justin_ending_someday.023: Not as a bit. Not because it's five a.m. and a building said goodnight to us. I like you exactly.
justin_ending_someday.024: I've liked you since a doorway, I think. I just thought it was about my footwork.
justin_ending_someday.025: He holds your eyes while he says it. He doesn't cover it with anything, and his hands stay where they are.
justin_ending_someday.026: I like you too. Exactly. I wrote "good weird" in a ledger, and then spent three years not going back to check what I meant.
justin_ending_someday.029: He laughs again, and then it settles, and he's serious in the way he's serious about a turn.
justin_ending_someday.030: Here's my thing. You've seen it. I rush the slow parts. I get scared of the middle, so I jump to the end and do a flourish so nobody sees the wobble.
justin_ending_someday.031: I don't want to do that with this. I want to get there on the count. I want every bit of the middle.
justin_ending_someday.032: Is that okay? It's not a no. It's the opposite of a no. It's me trying to do one thing in my life at the right speed.
justin_ending_someday.033: "It's what I want too. I've never stayed anywhere long enough to let something take its time."
justin_ending_someday.034: You mean it. Every place you've lived, you left before anything had the chance to grow slowly. You'd like to see what that looks like.
justin_ending_someday.035: Then it's a first for both of us. Good. I hate being the only beginner in the room.
justin_ending_someday.036: "I'll count. Slower than you would. You can't arrive until I say five."
justin_ending_someday.037: You'll be so strict about it.
justin_ending_someday.038: Front desk. We don't do early.
justin_ending_someday.039: …Thank you. I mean it. I'd get there at two and ruin everything.
justin_ending_someday.040: Open your fist. Hold your hand out, flat, between you. Wait.
justin_ending_someday.041: He puts his hand over yours. Not holding. Resting, the weight shared exactly half and half.
justin_ending_someday.042: Neither of you moves it for a whole eight. That's the answer, and you both know what it says.
justin_ending_someday.043: So. A place, a time, a thing to bring. Songha says a plan isn't a plan without all three.
justin_ending_someday.044: November. The night of the showcase. After I've done the slow piece, in front of people, without apologising to the floor.
justin_ending_someday.045: There's a bench outside the laundromat, out front. It'll still be there. That place never closes.
justin_ending_someday.046: I'll come out the second I've changed. I'll bring the end of the song. It'll have one by then. I'll play it to you on six strings.
justin_ending_someday.048: Strawberry milk. One carton. Bought. With money. I want it on record that it was *bought*.
justin_ending_someday.051: He says it to you, not to the rail, and lets it stand.
justin_ending_someday.052: And then I'm going to ask you properly. The whole question. No hand thing.
justin_ending_someday.053: I can tell you the answer now.
justin_ending_someday.055: It's yes. Ask me in November anyway.
justin_ending_someday.056: He sits down on the bench, next to the glass card, and laughs quietly, shaking his head, one hand over his eyes for a second.
justin_ending_someday.057: You can't just give me the answer. I have nine weeks of middle to get through.
justin_ending_someday.058: …Nine weeks. Sixty-three days. That's seven eights and a pickup.
justin_ending_someday.060: No, let me have this one. It's a good count. It's the best one I've ever been given.
justin_ending_someday.061: You sit beside him. Tuesdays and Fridays you'll see him anyway; you're in a schedule, and it's a little binding. It isn't nine weeks of waiting. It's nine weeks of the part he usually skips.
justin_ending_someday.062: The sun clears the building across the street. The red square from the glass card slides across the concrete and up over both your sneakers.
justin_ending_someday.063: He doesn't take your hand. He sets his on the bench, palm up, a cover's width from yours, and leaves it there in the light.
justin_ending_someday.067: He holds the stairwell door, and you go down together, one step at a time. He doesn't rush a single one.
